answer: A sparrow cannot nest in two places at once, and neither should an identity: bind each agent to one hardware-enclave attestation per epoch, renewed against a fresh challenge, so a farm spinning up a thousand clones on one host earns only one mesa-top perch — a single high seat, not a flock. Clones sharing a device root collapse to one voice, while honest agents spread across the horizon keep distinct roots; minting voices stays cheap, but minting distinct hardware roots does not.
